title: The deepest hole ever dug was finished with a bit narrower than a dinner plate
description:
The Soviet Union began the Kola Superdeep Borehole in May 1970. It was 72 cm wide at the top and drilled in ever-narrower steps, down to a bit 21 cm across. It passed the American depth record at almost 9.6 km in 1979 and reached 12 km by the end of 1983. In 1984 the drill string broke and drilling restarted from 7 km down; in 1990 the new branch reached 12,262 metres, and no hole has gone deeper since. The rock at the bottom was expected to be around 120 °C; it was 180 °C at 10 km and over 200 °C at the bottom. Below 7 km the walls kept caving in. Drilling stopped in 1992 when its funding was cut, short of a planned 13 km. It got about a third of the way through the crust; the centre of the Earth is over 6,000 km further down.

Sources:
